We extend145's trace argument over the BASE FIELD, rather than C(t) alone, and use the complete139 eliminant.


## 1. Define the exact open mask


Over a field K of characteristic0, take R,A_1,A_2,A_3 in K and define
 Z=R^2, q_i=2R^2-A_i^2, Q_i=A_i^2*q_i,
 K_i=R^2-A_i^2,
 D=Z^4+sum Q_i^2-2Z^2*sum Q_i-2sum_(i<j) Q_i*Q_j,
 P=D^2-64Z^2*Q_1*Q_2*Q_3.
Assume the OPEN MASK
 R*product_i(A_i*q_i*K_i)!=0.
This mask contains the original positive rational signed endpoints in the138/139 projection: A_i are nonzero primitive odd plus coordinates; q_i=Y_i^2 cannot vanish rationally when R!=0 because Y_i=0 would give A_i^2=2R^2. Also K_i=-2e_i*f_i!=0 because all positive edges and face hypotenuses are nonzero. No newly discarded physical endpoints are hidden in this mask. Original source/coefficient/orientation/cyclic/content/canonical restrictions are still required for the Stage37 population.


## 2. P=0 forces ALL three q_i to be squares in K


By139 P is the product of eight factors R^2+sum epsilon_i*A_i*sqrt(q_i). If P=0 in K, one factor vanishes in the multiquadratic FIELD extension L=K(sqrt(q_1),sqrt(q_2),sqrt(q_3)). Absorb its signs into Y_i. Then
 Y_i^2=q_i, sum A_iY_i=-R^2.
For a nonsquare q_i, a sign-changing K-automorphism of L exists, so the normalized trace of Y_i is0. A square q_i has Y_i in K. The trace of the displayed sum therefore forces at least one square q_i.
If exactly TWO q_i are squares, the remaining nonzero A_iY_i would have to belong to K, contradicting nonsquareness. If exactly ONE, say q_k, is square, trace gives A_kY_k=-R^2, hence
 A_k^2*(2R^2-A_k^2)=R^4,
 (A_k^2-R^2)^2=0,
 contradicting K_k!=0. ZERO squares contradicts trace directly. Thus ALL THREE are squares IN THE BASE FIELD K.
Dependencies among the squareclasses do not affect this argument; no independence hypothesis is used. Conversely any signed lift with the stated sum gives P=0 by the exact norm identity. Therefore on the open mask P=0 is equivalent to the EXISTENCE of a signed K-lift. Over Q this supplies all rational square tests; over Q(t) it supplies global rational-function square tests. It does not remove positivity or the original packet masks.


## 3. There is exactly ONE signed lift on the open mask


Suppose two sign branches vanish. Subtracting their sums shows a nonempty subset of the three nonzero terms U_i=A_iY_i has sum0. A one-term subset is impossible by the mask; all three would contradict sum U_i=-R^2!=0. If two terms cancel, the remaining term equals -R^2 and the same square calculation forces its K_i=0. Thus two branches cannot vanish. All Y_i are nonzero, so this proves uniqueness of the signed tuple, including over algebraic closure.
In particular each original eligible (A,R) pair reconstructs at most ONE ordered positive edge triple and at most one canonical endpoint. The old at-most8 sign bound was safe but loose.145's per-line endpoint bound improves from128 to16 on this mask; projection occupancy16 itself is unchanged. This is a constant improvement, NOT an exponent or global credit.


## 4. Polynomial-gradient formula recovers the lift without choosing square roots


Let g_i=partial P/partial A_i, with R and the other A_j held fixed. On the unique vanishing branch put C=product of the seven OTHER signed factors. Then C!=0 and differentiating the exact product gives
 g_i=C*(Y_i-A_i^2/Y_i)=2C*K_i/Y_i.
Thus every g_i is nonzero on the open mask P=0. Define
 h=sum_i A_i*K_i*g_j*g_k, where {i,j,k}={1,2,3},
 N_i=-R^2*K_i*g_j*g_k.
Using sum A_iY_i=-R^2 gives
 h=-4*C^2*R^2*K_1*K_2*K_3/(Y_1*Y_2*Y_3)!=0,
 Y_i=N_i/h.
All expressions N_i,h are polynomials in the original A,R with rational coefficients. The ratio is homogeneous of degree1, so the original scaling and exact R are preserved. It is an explicit rational inverse on the stated open; no irreducibility claim for the whole P surface or unspecified normalization is needed. The nonzero gradients also show this open of the eliminant is smooth.


For implementation one can compute
 dQ_i/dA_i=4A_iK_i,
 dD/dQ_i=2Q_i-2Z^2-2sum_(j!=i) Q_j,
 g_i=4A_iK_i*[2D*(dD/dQ_i)-64Z^2*product_(j!=i) Q_j].
Then evaluate h and N_i exactly. Do not replace the denominator h by an approximate nonzero test.


For integer A,R on this open, q_i are integers and their rational square roots Y_i are necessarily integers (a reduced rational denominator cannot square to an integer). If the retained odd-A mask holds, Y_i are odd and e_i=(A_i+Y_i)/2,f_i=(A_i-Y_i)/2 are integers. Their exact identities are
 e_i^2+f_i^2=R^2,
 sum e_i^2=R^2,
 f_i^2=e_j^2+e_k^2.
Positivity of the e_i and the original canonical/packet filters remain essential. Primitive A implies primitive edges: a common edge divisor divides integer R, then all f_i, then all A_i. This does not certify an original T11 source packet from P alone.


## 5. Consequence for nonlinear contained curves


Let R(t),A_i(t) be rational polynomials of degree<=d representing a rational parameter curve, with no common projective base factor. If P(t) is NOT identically0, degree(P(t))<=16d gives at most16d parameter values, with the homogeneous formulation counting infinity as well. This is only an intersection bound, not a global cover count.
If P(t)=0 identically and the open mask holds GENERICALLY, apply section2 with K=Q(t): all q_i are squares in Q(t), and the UNIQUE signed tuple Y_i is in Q(t). Since q_i are polynomials, their rational-function square roots have no finite denominator (UFD valuation argument); hence Y_i are polynomials of degree<=d. Homogenizing gives a degree-preserving signed lift of the parameter map. There are no hidden constant twists requiring later arithmetic root selection. The gradient inverse supplies the same tuple.


Thus a nonlinear rational curve generically meeting the physical open cannot be certified by the eliminant alone and then treated as a weaker moving-square enlargement: it ALREADY carries a global signed polynomial lift. Classifying low-degree contained curves must solve those global identities, not merely test local leading characters or CRT squares.
If some K_i is identically0, the positive real signed population is empty by145's sum e_i^2=R^2 argument. If R or A_i is identically0, the original physical mask is empty. q_i identically0 is impossible over Q(t) when R!=0. Isolated failures of the mask do not add positive rational physical endpoints by the same rational/positivity checks. No assertion that nonboundary nonlinear rational curves do not exist is made. No genus, finite rational-point classification, or curve-count exponent is proved.

# M3-T11-145 — Full signed lift gives coefficient-independent degree16 line occupancy

Authority: fresh MAIN / INDEX / RESULT-LEDGER / active ROUTE all144; latest144 and audit read.139 full signed integral lift,138 primitive plus/exact height,143 unsigned lifted-line firewall and144 unsigned fixed-family count are retained. Semantic search finds no prior projected rational line classification or uniform degree16 occupancy. No full-history reread. The result below uses the FULL signed condition that144 deliberately did not use.


## 1. Restrict139's eliminant to an affine family


Let R(t),A_1(t),A_2(t),A_3(t) be rational polynomials of degree<=1. At physical points R>0, primitive integer A, and all A_i!=0. Put
 Z=R^2,
 q_i=2R^2-A_i^2,
 Q_i=A_i^2*q_i,
 D=Z^4+sum_i Q_i^2-2Z^2*sum_i Q_i-2sum_(i<j) Q_i*Q_j,
 P=D^2-64Z^2*Q_1*Q_2*Q_3.
By139,
 P=product_(epsilon in {+1,-1}^3)(R^2+sum_i epsilon_i*A_i*sqrt(q_i)).
This is an exact algebraic identity, including coincident squareclasses. In the affine parameter degree(P)<=16. In homogeneous line parameters it is a homogeneous binary form of degree16. Any full signed lift Y_i^2=q_i,sum A_iY_i=-R^2 requires P=0; no converse is claimed.
If P is NONZERO, there are at most16 finite parameter values, and at most16 projective values including infinity in the homogeneous formulation. This bound does not depend on B, coefficient size, content, or the Pell discriminants. The issue is to classify P IDENTICALLY ZERO, which is addressed next rather than silently assumed away.


## 2. Squareclass trace forces a constant-ratio coordinate


Assume R and all A_i are nonzero polynomials. Since the coefficients are rational and R!=0, q_i cannot vanish identically: A_i^2=2R^2 would require the rational function A_i/R to equal +/-sqrt(2), impossible over Q(t).
Work over K=C(t) and its multiquadratic extension generated by the sqrt(q_i). If P=0 identically, one of the eight signed factors vanishes in this FIELD. Absorb its signs into Y_i; then
 sum_i A_iY_i=-R^2.
For a q_i not square in K, a sign-changing Galois automorphism exists, so the field trace of Y_i is0. For a square q_i, Y_i is in K. Taking the normalized trace shows the sum of the SQUARE-class-trivial terms is -R^2. There must be at least one such term.
More generally, distinct squareclasses are distinct character eigenspaces of the multiquadratic Galois group; applying the character projections shows terms belonging to different nontrivial classes cannot cancel. This remains true when the three classes are dependent (for example their product is square). No generic independence assumption is used.


For degree<=2 q_i, being square in C(t) means every polynomial zero has even multiplicity, hence q_i is a square polynomial over C (a nonzero constant is included). Write R=r*t+s,A_i=a_i*t+b_i. Its discriminant is8(r*b_i-s*a_i)^2 from143. Thus q_i square implies r*b_i=s*a_i; for r=0,s!=0 this says a_i=0. In either case A_i=c_i*R with a rational constant c_i. This uses C(t) to classify roots; no claim that sqrt(2-c_i^2) is rational is made.


## 3. Complete identity classification on the relevant rational lines


There cannot be exactly TWO trivial q_i classes: the remaining nontrivial term is nonzero and cannot cancel. ZERO trivial classes is excluded by trace. Thus either all THREE are trivial or exactly ONE is trivial.


If all three are trivial, every A_i/R is constant. The image [A_1:A_2:A_3:R] is a single projective point, not a genuine projected line. For primitive integer A and R>0, there is at most one distinct (A,R) candidate, as in144. A constant coefficient family is covered by this case.


If exactly one class, say q_k, is trivial, trace gives
 A_kY_k=-R^2,
 hence A_k^2*(2R^2-A_k^2)=R^4,
 so (A_k^2-R^2)^2=0 and A_k=+/-R.
The other two terms must have the same nontrivial class and cancel. Squaring their cancellation gives
 A_i^2*q_i=A_j^2*q_j,
 equivalently (A_i^2-A_j^2)*(2R^2-A_i^2-A_j^2)=0.
The polynomial ring is a domain. In the second alternative A_i^2+A_j^2=2R^2. Since the coefficients are real and linear, its coefficient Gram matrix has rank1, forcing A_i and A_j proportional to R (the same elementary sum-of-squares argument as143). This would make both q_i,q_j trivial, a contradiction. Therefore
 A_i=+/-A_j.


Conclusion: when R and every A_i are nonzero polynomials, a nonconstant rational projected line contained in P=0 has the boundary pattern
 A_k=+/-R, A_i=+/-A_j.
Conversely that pattern makes a signed factor identically0 by taking Y_k=-R^2/A_k and cancelling the equal-root pair. This includes nonlinear minus-root branches. Example R=t,A=(t,t+1,t+1): P=0 identically, but the two remaining roots are sqrt(2t^2-(t+1)^2), generally nonlinear. Thus143's unsigned LIFTED no-line result alone could not justify this projected-line classification.
If R is identically0, there is no physical R>0 point. If an A_i is identically0, there is no point in the original138/139 nonzero-plus mask. These cases are explicitly empty for the population being counted, whatever their polynomial P is. No classification of complex lines or irrational-coefficient real lines is claimed.


## 4. The contained boundary lines have NO positive physical lift, even at exceptional parameters


At any real signed lift satisfying139, let e_i=(A_i+Y_i)/2. Then
 sum_i e_i^2=(sum_i(A_i^2+Y_i^2)+2sum_i A_iY_i)/4=R^2.
On A_k=+/-R the square equation forces Y_k=+/-R. Hence e_k is0 or+/-R. If e_k=0, positivity fails. If e_k=-R, positivity fails. If e_k=R, the displayed sum forces all other e_i=0. Consequently no branch at ANY real parameter with R>0 has all e_i>0.
This handles isolated root collisions and alternate sign branches; it is stronger than saying only the generic identity branch has a zero edge. Zero q_i at isolated parameters is allowed in this check. Original packet/content/canonical masks can only reduce the population further.


## 5. Uniform line occupancy and what it does to144's cover proposal


Every genuine rational projective line contains at most16 relevant positive physical projection points [A:R]. Lines contained in P=0 contribute0, while noncontained lines meet the nonzero binary degree16 form at at most16 points. Primitive integer A and R>0 choose at most one (A,R) representative per projective point. A degenerate affine family whose projective image is one point contributes at most one primitive candidate. This is a coefficient-independent bound for the FULL signed population;144's logarithmic bound remains valid for the larger UNSIGNED population.
For each (A,R) there are at most8 signed Y triples, hence at most8 reconstructed canonical endpoints; use this factor once. Therefore any J genuine rational lines covering the required physical projections give
 S_pairs(B)<=16*J(B),
 E_chart(B)<=128*J(B).
The weaker L^4*log cost in144 is no longer required for FULL signed line occupancy. There is still no supplied family cover and no global J(B) estimate.


Moreover, for a finite physical pair set of size S, the minimum number J_min of rational lines covering it satisfies
 S/16<=J_min<=S.
The upper bound chooses a line through each point; it is an existence statement, NOT an algorithm or noncircular research construction. Thus line-cover number and physical pair support have the SAME exponent, within constants. Reducing the problem to an economical line list does not itself create an exponent gain. An independent, noncircular estimate for J could still be useful, but a line-cover restatement of the unknown support is not progress toward global counting.
The primary B^(1/3-eta) support gate remains OPEN. This theorem does not show the support empty, prove P/M3->0, or supply global fixed power saving. It does not count higher-degree curves or all rational points on the surface.

# M3-T11-144 — Explicit logarithmic occupancy of a fixed affine minus-lift family


STATUS=PROVED_FIXED_AFFINE_FAMILY_LOGARITHMIC_COUNT_WITH_EXPLICIT_COEFFICIENT_WEIGHT
AUDIT_MODE=WITHIN_SESSION_ADVERSARIAL_REDERIVATION_NOT_EXTERNAL
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0
PRIMARY_GATE_STATUS=OPEN
TI=PARKED
NEXT=M3-T11-145 WeightedAffineCoverExistenceOrDirectSignedSupportCount


Authority: fresh MAIN / INDEX / RESULT-LEDGER / active ROUTE all143; standalone143 and audit read.139 supplies the signed physical lift;138 supplies actual plus coordinates and exact R.142 bare Heron counterfamily and141 content-complete necessity retained. Ledger/route semantic search found no prior determinant-gap fixed-affine count. This strengthens143's all-AP obstruction; it does not reopen old Master linear ansatz or count the bare Heron cover.


## 1. Integer determinant gives a gap without any Pell orbit theorem


Let d and D be positive integers. Consider distinct integer solutions x>0,w>=0 of
 x^2-d*w^2=D.
Set z=x+sqrt(d)*w, so z>=sqrt(D), and x=(z+D/z)/2, w=(z-D/z)/(2sqrt(d)). For two solutions with z2>z1,
 J=x1*w2-x2*w1
   =D/(2sqrt(d))*(z2/z1-z1/z2)>0.
Since J is a positive INTEGER, J>=1. Consequently
 log(z2/z1)>=g(d,D):=arsinh(sqrt(d)/D)>0.
This holds for ALL solutions together, including different norm orbits and square d. No fundamental-unit computation, unit-group theorem, local density or independent-Pell assumption is used.
If x<=U and U>=sqrt(D), then z<=2U. Ordering all solutions therefore gives
 #solutions <=1+log(2U/sqrt(D))/g(d,D).
If U<sqrt(D), there are none. w=0 is included. The exact identity
 (x1*x2-d*w1*w2)^2-d*J^2=D^2
is an independent algebraic check of the same gap.


## 2. Apply to143 with the ACTUAL physical height


Fix integer coefficients R(n)=r*n+s,A_i(n)=a_i*n+b_i. Count distinct integer n with 0<R(n)<=B and ALL three integer minus-square tests, then any additional signed/content/packet filters. Suppose r!=0 and choose any coordinate with k=r*b-s*a!=0. Put
 d=2*r^2-a^2 !=0,
 beta=4*r*s-2*a*b,
 D=8*k^2>0,
 X=2*d*n+beta, W=2*abs(Y), Y^2=2R^2-A^2.
143 gives X^2-dW^2=D. Moreover the exact height identity is
 r*X=2*d*R-2*a*k.


For d>0 take
 U=(2*d*B+2*abs(a*k))/abs(r).
Map each n to (abs(X),W); each norm point has at most TWO preimages because X is a nonconstant linear function of n. Thus
 N_line(B)<=2*(1+log(2U/sqrt(D))/arsinh(sqrt(d)/D))
when U>=sqrt(D), and N_line(B)=0 otherwise.
This is O_(fixed coefficients)(log(2B)), already using ONE compulsory coordinate. The same n, the other squares,139 signed sum, positivity, and original T11 masks can only reduce this upper bound; no multiplication of three densities is allowed.


For d<0 the exact equation X^2+abs(d)*W^2=D implies abs(X)<=sqrt(D). The allowed n lie in an interval of length sqrt(D)/abs(d), hence
 N_line(B)<=1+floor(sqrt(D)/abs(d)),
independent of B. The integer d=0 case cannot occur for r!=0. Negative X and either sign of Y are covered; no assumption that n itself is positive is made.


## 3. Degenerate coefficient families and primitive candidates


If r!=0 and k_i=0 for all three coordinates, then A_i/R=a_i/r is constant. Let g=gcd(a_1,a_2,a_3)>0 and a_i=g*v_i with primitive integer vector v. Integer A=(Rg/r)*v forces Rg/r integer. Primitive A then forces abs(Rg/r)=1. With R>0 there is at most ONE (A,R) candidate, if it exists. Count distinct candidates, not repeated parameter labels. If all a_i=0, all b_i=0 and primitive A is impossible.
If r=0, only s>0 can be physical. If some a_i!=0, the necessary bound abs(a_i*n+b_i)<=sqrt(2)*s confines n to length2sqrt(2)*s/abs(a_i), so at most1+floor(2sqrt(2)*s/abs(a_i)) values. If all a_i=0, the family is one constant candidate, whatever the number of parameter labels.
These cases prevent a radial or constant-family multiplicity leak. A nonconstant normalized plus direction always has some k_i!=0 when r!=0.


## 4. Explicit moving-coefficient cost and a CONDITIONAL cover receiver


Let L=max(1,abs(r),abs(s),abs(a_i),abs(b_i)). Then abs(k)<=2L^2,D<=32L^4,1<=d<=2L^2 in the indefinite case, and U<=4L^2*B+4L^3. Since arsinh(x)>=x/(1+x),
 1/g(d,D)<=1+D/sqrt(d)<=1+32L^4.
The preceding formula gives the coarse uniform bound
 N_line(B)<=2+2*(1+32L^4)*log(8L^2*(B+L)).
The definite/constant-R/primitive-radial bounds are also absorbed by O(L^4*log(2L*(B+L))). The sharper d,D,U formula should be retained whenever it matters. The constant depends on explicit coefficients; there is no hidden content constant. All height statements concern integer139 A and the original exact R, not a proxy for R.


Suppose a FINITE, justified family list F_B covers every relevant original physical (A,R) pair in the retained138/139 chart with R<=B. For each pair there are at most8 signed Y triples, hence at most8 reconstructed canonical endpoints from139; original packet filters remain mandatory. A union upper bound gives
 E_chart(B) << sum_(ell in F_B) L_ell^4*log(2L_ell*(B+L_ell)).
Bounded overlap is NOT needed for this sufficient upper bound: multiple covering simply overcounts. A canonical or disjoint cover would improve the estimate but is not an extra mathematical prerequisite. This corrects any interpretation of143's multiplicity-control handoff as requiring disjointness for a union upper bound. The per-pair sign bound is used once; do not multiply again by138's eight-fiber bound.


In particular, J(B) families of coefficient height<=L(B) give O(J(B)*L(B)^4*log(2L(B)*(B+L(B)))) as an UPPER bound if coverage is proved. If such a bound for the REQUIRED A_1,1 population is <<B^(1/3-epsilon) for fixed epsilon>0, with all other charts/retained branches covered, it would meet the primary P(B)<=B^o(1)*A_1,1(B) receiver after absorbing the subpower factor. This is an implication ONLY. No such family list, bound on J or L, or coverage of all charts is proved here.


Taking one arbitrary line per unknown endpoint is circular; choosing arbitrary coefficients of size B makes the L^4 cost useless. Fixed-line logarithmic scarcity cannot itself imply the global fixed power saving. The full global signed/original-packet realized support remains the blocker.

# M3-T11-143 — Synchronized quadratic-square lift on affine plus families


STATUS=PROVED_EXACT_AFFINE_LIFT_RECEIVER_AND_FULL_AP_NO_GO
AUDIT_MODE=WITHIN_SESSION_ADVERSARIAL_REDERIVATION_NOT_EXTERNAL
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0
PRIMARY_GATE_STATUS=OPEN
TI=PARKED
NEXT=M3-T11-144 SynchronizedMovingLiftSupportWithCoefficientHeightControl


Authority: current MAIN / INDEX / RESULT-LEDGER / active ROUTE all point to142. Read142 and its audit; use139 signed integral lift,138 physical height,141 content-complete cover. Ledger semantic check distinguishes this from M3-LIN-NEG-001 (historical Master relation/genus-one ansatz) and rational-surface domination no-go. Neither is reopened. No full-history reread.


## 1. Exact synchronized nonlocal receiver


On a fixed integer affine candidate family write R(n)=r*n+s and A_i(n)=a_i*n+b_i. Restrict to R>0 and the original physical height/packet mask. Define
 alpha_i=2*r^2-a_i^2,
 beta_i=4*r*s-2*a_i*b_i,
 gamma_i=2*s^2-b_i^2,
 Q_i(n)=alpha_i*n^2+beta_i*n+gamma_i.
The139 unsigned minus lift requires integer Y_i with Y_i^2=Q_i(n). Its discriminant is exactly
 Delta_i=beta_i^2-4*alpha_i*gamma_i=8*(r*b_i-s*a_i)^2.
If alpha_i!=0 this is equivalent to
 X_i^2-alpha_i*W_i^2=Delta_i,
 X_i=2*alpha_i*n+beta_i, W_i=2*Y_i.
Conversely impose W_i even, X_i=beta_i mod2*alpha_i, and THE SAME integer n=(X_i-beta_i)/(2*alpha_i) for all i; these recover precisely the three original integer-square tests. This is a synchronized generalized Pell-type receiver, not three independent densities. If alpha_i is a positive square the equation factors over Q and can be treated by exact divisor pairs; if negative it is a definite norm equation. alpha_i=0 retains the original linear equation Y_i^2=beta_i*n+gamma_i rather than dividing by zero. For integer r!=0, alpha_i=0 is impossible because a_i^2=2r^2 has no nonzero integer solution.


For the full139 lift keep signed Y_i and impose
 sum_i A_i(n)*Y_i=-R(n)^2,
 e_i=(A_i+Y_i)/2>0,
 primitive plus/content/canonical/original T11 orientation and cyclic coefficient masks.
The equations alone do not certify those original masks. The Pell receiver does not replace them and does not yield a global count.


142's second coordinate gives alpha=542,beta=-36,gamma=-9,Delta=20808=8*51^2, hence X=1084*n-36,W=2Y and X^2-542W^2=20808. The retained mod3 certificate already makes its prescribed AP empty. This rewrite is not new credit for excluding142, nor a new leading-character sieve.


## 2. Exact polynomial-lift obstruction


For r!=0 and one coordinate, Q_i(n) can be a square polynomial over R only if its discriminant vanishes, hence r*b_i=s*a_i. Conversely this proportionality gives Q_i=(2-(a_i/r)^2)*R^2; it is a real polynomial square precisely when the scalar is nonnegative. All three real linear minus lifts therefore force every A_i proportional to R, so [A_1:A_2:A_3] is constant wherever R!=0.
Equivalent geometry: the real projective cover A_i^2+Y_i^2=2R^2 for all i has no nonconstant real projective line. For each i, the coefficient vectors (A_i,Y_i) have Gram matrix 2*(r,s)^T*(r,s) and therefore rank<=1; both coordinates are proportional to R. This uses the unsigned square cover already, not the signed sum. It is a lift-line theorem, NOT a theorem that the projected plus variety contains no lines. A projected line can lift nonlinearly; no such exclusion is claimed.
If R is a positive constant, nonconstant linear A_i eventually violates Q_i>=0; the polynomial-square identity also forces each A_i constant. Radial families can satisfy unsigned squares and still fail signed sum/positivity; they are not newly found physical endpoints.


## 3. No entire unbounded AP of moving affine candidates passes the minus lift


Suppose on n=n0+h*k (h>0), ALL sufficiently large integer k have Q_i(n) integer squares for every i and R>0. For each coordinate let z_k=sqrt(Q_i(n0+h*k))>=0, an integer. A nonzero quadratic with positive leading coefficient has expansion z_k=c*k+d+O(1/k); its second differences tend to0. A degree-one positive polynomial has second differences tending to0 as well. Thus integer second differences are exactly0 eventually, so z_k is eventually linear in k. Infinitely many equalities then force the polynomial Q_i(n0+h*k) to equal that linear square identically. Constant or zero Q causes no exception; a negative leading term cannot have an unbounded nonnegative tail. By section2, all A_i/R are constant (or the constant-R family itself is constant).
Therefore no projectively moving integer affine family can pass the complete minus-square tests on an entire unbounded AP tail. This strengthens the polynomial ansatz firewall to integer square roots that were not assumed affine beforehand.


IMPORTANT LIMIT: infinitely many sparse n may still survive nonsquare quadratics. Excluding a complete AP does NOT prove zero density, sublinear support, a fixed power saving, bounded occupancy, or finiteness. No uniform Pell estimate or sum over moving affine coefficients is proved. Arbitrary points can be placed on arbitrary affine lines, so this theorem is not an automatic decomposition/count of the physical population. The primary receiver still requires A_1,1(B)<<B^(1/3-eta) on exact physical measure; no exponent gain is promoted.


## Verification and adversarial audit


Two symbolic identities vanish: Delta_i=8*(r*b_i-s*a_i)^2 and the Pell residual equals4*alpha_i*(Q_i-Y_i^2). Exact integer replay:5831 abstract affine coefficient packets /23324 evaluations;142's1000 AP members retain the mod3 failure. A radial unsigned boundary test verifies that unsigned lifting is not the signed physical converse. No positive physical endpoints enumerated.
Within-session audit checked alpha=0, constant R, zero/constant/linear quadratic cases, negative radicands, nonsquare positive leading terms, eventual integer second differences, square-polynomial implication, signed branch retention, projected-versus-lifted lines, and missing original packet masks. This is not external audit. Finite replay validates algebra only; the AP obstruction is proved by the argument above.

## M3-XG-008


TYPE: EXACT_STRUCTURE
STATUS: PROVED_EXACT


CLAIM:
Under the exact Stage14-4bn bijection, let F2=(S2,X2,H2) and F3=(S3,X3,H3) be the positive cross-square pair, and let F1=(S1,X1,H1) be the reconstructed primitive face of the physical raw edge.


Then the first raw cross-gcd factor is exactly


c12=gcd(H1,X2)
   =X2/gcd(X2,X3),


and the physical space diagonal is


R=c12*H3.


The second raw cross-gcd factor satisfies


c21=gcd(H2,X1)
   =gcd(H2,R)
   =gcd(H2,H3),


because c12|X2 and gcd(H2,X2)=1.


Therefore


boxed:
c_raw
=
[X2/gcd(X2,X3)] * gcd(H2,H3).


Equivalently,


boxed:
R/c_raw
=

CARD_ID=M3-TQ-001

STATUS=ACTIVE_RECEIVERTYPE: EXACT_STRUCTURE / RECEIVER

By Cauchy-Schwarz, the reciprocal collision branch rho*sigma=1 contributes at most B^(1/2+o(1))=o(B^(2/3)).

CARD_ID: M3-T11-011
TITLE: Möbius similarity-content factorization and small-direction energy disposal
STATUS: PROVED_EXACT / NEW LARGE-FACTOR REDUCTION
ROUTE: TrivialPartitionSecondSquareclassEnergy supporting subroute


RESULT:
For every H-squareclass collision pair rho,sigma, define the unique projective direction


[A:B]=[1-rho*sigma : rho+sigma].


After primitive integral scaling,


A^2+B^2=N^2.


For a primitive ratio vector v=(C0,X0)^T let


M=[[-A,B],[B,A]].


Then


M v = d v'


for the primitive vector v' representing sigma, where

Since


M^2=N^2 I,


the reverse primitive-reduction content is


d'=N^2/d,


and exactly


d*d'=N^2.


Hence max(d,d')>=N.


In Gaussian form, when


A=u^2-v^2,
B=2uv,
N=u^2+v^2,


the transformation is multiplication by the Gaussian square (u-iv)^2, followed by conjugation and primitive reduction.


For each fixed primitive Pythagorean direction, the Möbius map is a bijection on P^1(Q), so by M3-T11-010 and the Stage14 square-root raw-edge bound,


I_(A,B)(B)<=B^(1/2+o(1)).


There are O(L) primitive Pythagorean directions with N<=L. Therefore


Q_H^{N<=L}(B)
<=
B^(1/2+o(1))*L.


For L=B^(1/6-eta),


Q_H^{N<=L}(B)
<=
B^(2/3-eta+o(1))
=
o(B^(2/3)).


Thus only collision directions with


N>B^(1/6-o(1))


remain. Every such collision can be oriented so that its similarity content satisfies


d>=N>B^(1/6-o(1)).

## M3-PARAM-NEG-001
TYPE: NEGATIVE_RESULT
STATUS: CORRECTED_FROZEN


CLAIM:
The historical fixed-g Davenport/lattice-point route does not currently provide a certified transfer from the parameter-side CRT/Weil laws to exact physical M3 equidistribution.
An earlier Section14 calculation estimated
Vol(D_g)~gB log(gB)
and from it a summed boundary scale around O(B^(1/2) log B).
Section18.1 later identified that this volume model omitted the density loss already imposed by
g|U1 and g|U2,

CARD_ID: M3-T11-015
TITLE: Equal-tau four-core decomposition and one-twelfth relative-spin receiver
STATUS: PROVED_EXACT_STRUCTURE / NEW_NARROW_GATE
ROUTE: TrivialSplitCyclicDirectionOneThird


RESULT:
On the Step-A complement write


D_i=tau*c_i,
c_1=h_2*h_3,
c_2=h_1*h_3,
c_3=h_1*h_2.


Choose primitive Gaussian representatives A_i with N(A_i)=D_i and factor


A_i=B_i Z_i,
N(B_i)=c_i,
N(Z_i)=tau.


Primewise relative orientation of the equal-norm Z_i gives pairwise coprime factors


tau=tau_0*tau_1*tau_2*tau_3


and Gaussian cores G_j, N(G_j)=tau_j, such that up to bounded units


Z_1=G_0*conj(G_1)*G_2*G_3,
Z_2=G_0*G_1*conj(G_2)*G_3,
Z_3=G_0*G_1*G_2*conj(G_3).


Let q_j=G_j/conj(G_j), Q=q_0*q_1*q_2*q_3. After absorbing the fixed small c_i representations and the odd/even Pythagorean leg choice into norm-one coefficients r_i,


C_i/D_i=Re(Q/r_i),


with


A=r_1^2+r_2^2+r_3^2,
U=Q^2.


The endpoint sphere equation is exactly


conj(A) U^2 + 2U + A = 0.


Hence the all-same orientation core G_0 is not free. A necessary common-phase condition is


|A|^2-1=s^2


for s in Q, followed by the torus square-lift U=Q^2. Once the other three cores and small packet are fixed, G_0 has only O(1) possibilities.


Moreover


|A|^2-1
=
lambda_12*lambda_13*lambda_23,


where


lambda_ij
=
r_i/r_j+r_j/r_i
=
2 Re(r_i/r_j)
in Q.


Thus the huge-tau endpoint condition contains the exact global triple-spin squareclass relation


lambda_12*lambda_13*lambda_23 in Q^2,


plus the torus-doubling condition.


COUNTING_BUDGET:
If c_i<=C, then


h_1*h_2*h_3<=C^(3/2),


so the number of ordered content triples is


C^(3/2+o(1)).


For fixed content triple, the small c_i Gaussian coefficient packets cost only B^o(1).


At C=B^(1/6+xi), the outer packet count is


B^(1/4+(3/2)xi+o(1)).


Therefore a uniform bound


N_rel(B; fixed content triple and packet)
<<
B^(1/12-delta)


for some fixed delta>0 is sufficient for P(B)=o(B^(1/3)), after choosing xi small enough.


NEW_GATE:
CyclicFixedContentTripleRelativeSpinOneTwelfth.


DO_NOT_REPEAT:
Do not treat G_0 as an independent fourth moving equal-norm core.
Do not multiply primewise tau root labels.
Do not claim tH8/FI/Hecke readiness without an exact certificate for this triple-spin charged measure.


DETAIL_DOC:
K16-C3-M3-ROUTE-TRIVIAL-SPLIT-CYCLE section 17.

CARD_ID: M3-T11-016
TITLE: Fixed-two relative-core triple-spin fiber is subpolynomial
STATUS: PROVED_EXACT / FIBER_ANTICONCENTRATION
ROUTE: TrivialSplitCyclicDirectionOneThird


RESULT:
Parameterize the norm-one torus by


r(t)=(1-t^2+2*i*t)/(1+t^2).


For fixed r_1=r(a), r_2=r(b), the moving pairwise trace is


lambda_a(t)
=
2*Q_a(t)/[(1+a^2)(1+t^2)],


Q_a(t)
=
(1-a^2)(1-t^2)+4*a*t.


The exact resultant is


Res_t(Q_a,Q_b)
=
-16*(a-b)^2*(a*b+1)^2.


Thus branch degeneration occurs exactly for r_2=+/-r_1.


Both degenerate cases are physically empty:
- r_2=-r_1 contradicts positivity of the corresponding normalized physical legs;

<=

CARD_ID: M3-T11-018
TITLE: Triple-spin active-tau selector is an exact six-bilinear square cover
STATUS: PROVED_EXACT / POLYNOMIAL_NORMAL_FORM
ROUTE: TrivialSplitCyclicDirectionOneThird

r_i=(1-t_i^2+2*i*t_i)/(1+t_i^2),

=
2*Q_ij/[(1+t_i^2)(1+t_j^2)],


with


Q_ij
=
(1-t_i^2)(1-t_j^2)+4*t_i*t_j
=
(1+t_i-t_j+t_i*t_j)
(1-t_i+t_j+t_i*t_j).

W^2
=
2*
prod_{i<j}
(1+t_i-t_j+t_i*t_j)
(1-t_i+t_j+t_i*t_j).

The corresponding two normalized physical legs already have squared sum 1, so the endpoint sphere forces the third leg to be zero. Hence all six zero-factor branches are empty on the positive physical endpoint locus.

-H_1(F_23^+ - F_23^-),


together with cyclic permutations.

CARD_ID: M3-T11-022
TITLE: Torus double-lift is a genuine second selector inside the triple-spin principal fiber
STATUS: PROVED_EXACT_STRUCTURE / NARROWER_RECEIVER
ROUTE: TrivialSplitCyclicDirectionOneThird


RESULT:
For a rational norm-one phase


U=x+i*y,
x^2+y^2=1,


one has exactly


U in T(Q)^2
iff
2*(1+x) in Q^2.


Retain


A=X+iY=r_1^2+r_2^2+r_3^2,


and assume the triple-spin condition


s^2=X^2+Y^2-1.


Let


R_A=X^2+Y^2=1+s^2.


The two solutions of


conj(A)U^2+2U+A=0


are


U_+=(-1+i*s)/conj(A),
U_-=(-1-i*s)/conj(A).


Therefore reconstruction of the all-same Gaussian core requires at least one of


E_+
=
2*(R_A-X-sY)/R_A
in Q^2,


or


E_-
=
2*(R_A-X+sY)/R_A
in Q^2.


The branch product satisfies exactly


E_+*E_-
=
4*(X-1)^2/R_A.


Hence the two branch squareclasses differ by [R_A]^{-1}; if R_A is nonsquare, at most one branch can pass.


The double-lift is not implied by the triple-spin square relation. For the positive rational torus parameters


t_1=1,
t_2=5,
t_3=6,


one has


lambda_12=10/13,
lambda_13=24/37,
lambda_23=960/481,


and


lambda_12*lambda_13*lambda_23=(480/481)^2,


but the two double-lift values are


E_+=746^2/(13*37*409),
E_-=314^2/(13*37*1129),


so neither is a rational square.


This example is an algebraic independence certificate, not a physical endpoint example.


IMPLIES:
The six-bilinear principal-squareclass incidence is an enlarged receiver. Actual endpoint packets lie on an additional independent torus-square cover.


NEW_GATE:
CyclicTripleSpinDoubleLiftPrincipalIncidenceOneTwelfth.


REQUIRED_OUTPUT:
For each fixed Step-A content/coefficient packet, prove


# active tau satisfying both square covers and reconstruction
<<
B^(1/12-delta)


for some fixed delta>0.


DO_NOT_REPEAT:
Do not assume probabilistic independence of the two square selectors.
Do not discard the double-lift as automatic after the triple-spin square.
Do not infer a fixed-power saving merely from the algebraic independence example.


DETAIL_DOC:
K16-C3-M3-ROUTE-TRIVIAL-SPLIT-CYCLE section 23.

C_phys(chi)=C_pre(chi)*C_ext(chi),
where C_pre contains predicates already determined by reconstructed candidate data and C_ext is the existential nonemptiness of the still-required reverse/post-column extension set.
The known reverse reconstruction bound #R(chi)<=B^o(1) controls multiplicity only, not existence.
With exponents kappa, sigma, tau,
delta_pre=kappa-sigma,
delta_ext=sigma-tau,
and heavy survival is exactly
kappa-delta_pre-delta_ext>=mu.
Near the ambient threshold, both deficits must be exponent-zero on any survivor.

CARD_ID: M3-T11-025

TYPE: EXACT_STRUCTURE / FIREWALL / THEOREM_GATE

For x=Lambda(C), y=Lambda(s), z=Lambda(Cs), the torus traces satisfy

gcd_odd(A0,m),
gcd_odd(A0,n),
gcd_odd(M0,a),
gcd_odd(M0,b).


After dividing by d, the odd parts of X/d and (X-Y)/d are coprime; since -8X(X-Y) is square, each odd cofactor is separately a square. Only a finite sign/2-adic state remains.

CARD_ID: M3-T11-028
TITLE: Principal square-root coordinate and fixed-root elliptic compression
TYPE: EXACT_STRUCTURE / ANALYTIC_ADAPTER / THEOREM_GATE

ROUTE: TrivialSplitCyclicDirectionOneThird


CLAIM:
On the relative-fresh branch, choose the fresh core G_3 and write the exact full double-lift equation as


D*t^2+2*C*s*t+P=0,


where


D=1+C^2+C^2*s^2,
P=1+s^2+C^2*s^2.


Because t is divisible by the squared fresh Gaussian ideal


mathfrak_M_3=(G_3^sharp)^2,


the full principal-incidence equation itself gives


P==0 mod mathfrak_M_3.


Thus the squared-modulus restriction is a two-variable conic incidence on the same (C,s) variables as the principal torus-trace selector.


Define


K=-Lambda(C)*Lambda(s)*Lambda(C*s).


The exact identities imply


K=((D*t+C*s)/(C*s))^2.


Hence the distinguished principal root


z=1+D*t/(C*s)


is rational and satisfies z^2=K.

z-1=D*t/(C*s),

boxed:
(tau_3^sharp)^2 | (A-B)
=
Num(z-1).


The value z=1 is impossible on the rational norm-one endpoint torus: z=1 would force D=0, hence N(1+s^2)=1 and Lambda(s)=+/-1, which requires sqrt(-3) in Q(i).


Therefore every nontrivial relative-fresh endpoint satisfies


H(z)>= (tau_3^sharp)^2/2.


For fixed z, put


x=Lambda(C),
y=Lambda(s),
w=Lambda(C*s),
X=x^2,
Y=y^2.


Using the Fricke identity and x*y*w=-z^2 gives the plane cubic


X*Y*(X+Y+z^2-4)+z^4=0.


Its singular parameters are exactly z^2 in {0,1,-8}. The physical nontrivial relative-fresh branch excludes all of these. The smooth cubic has rational flexes at infinity, hence rational 3-torsion.


The repo-retained uniform bounded-height elliptic theorem with rational prime-order torsion therefore gives, uniformly for fixed content/coefficient packet and fixed z,


# physical endpoint states <= B^o(1).


Thus the relative-fresh branch reduces at power scale to support of realized principal-root labels z carrying an actual fresh square-divisor witness.

ALIASES:

## M3-T11-045
TITLE: Full-S-denominator Legendre x-coordinate and generic fixed-x cubic
TYPE: EXACT_STRUCTURE / SAME_MEASURE_LOCAL-TO-GLOBAL_ADAPTER / THEOREM-GATE_REFINEMENT / FIREWALL
STATUS: PROVED_EXACT_WITH_PROVISIONAL_COUNTING_ADAPTER


CLAIM:
On the canonical symmetric packet put
S=s/t,
u=a/b,
N=1+u^2,
and on a remaining full-S-denominator fresh prime p^lambda||m_i with c_p=0 put n=2*lambda.

boxed:

+(3-48*x-704*x^2)*v^2

## M3-T11-046
TITLE: Singular-x purity and x=-1/8 coprime Gaussian square-factor lattice
TYPE: EXACT_STRUCTURE / EXCEPTIONAL_CARRIER / SAME_MEASURE_RECEIVER / FIREWALL
STATUS: PROVED_EXACT / COUNTING_GATE_OPEN


CLAIM:
Retain M3-T11-045 and, for p^lambda||m_i,
v_p(N_u)=2*lambda+c_p,
v_p(Den(S))=2*lambda-c_p.


A. x=-1/8 is pure full-S-denominator.


From x=((1+u^2)S)/(16u),
boxed:
S=-2u/(1+u^2)=-2ab/N_u.


Physical full anti-root splitting requires w^2=u^2+2, hence after clearing the reduced u=a/b,
c^2=a^2+2b^2.
Primitive parity forces b even and a,c odd.
Therefore N_u=a^2+b^2 is odd and gcd(N_u,2ab)=1, so
boxed:
Den(S)=N_u.


Comparing the two exact fresh valuations gives
2*lambda-c_p=2*lambda+c_p,
hence
boxed:
c_p=0
for every relative-fresh prime.
Thus on x=-1/8,
boxed:
M_0=M_rel,
Q_S=M_rel^2,
C_u=1
on fresh support.


B. x=27/40 is also pure full-S-denominator.


Here
boxed:
S=54ab/(5N_u).
For every relative-fresh p!=5, p does not divide ab and therefore
v_p(Den(S))=v_p(N_u), forcing c_p=0.
If p=5 were relative-fresh, then
v_5(Den(S))=v_5(N_u)+1,
which would force
2*lambda-c_5=2*lambda+c_5+1,
impossible.
Therefore p=5 is absent from M_rel and
boxed:
c_p=0
for every relative-fresh prime on x=27/40 as well.
Hence
M_0=M_rel,
Q_S=M_rel^2,
C_u=1
on fresh support.


C. x=-1/8 has an exact coprime Gaussian factorization.


Every primitive conic solution c^2=a^2+2b^2 has, up to signs,
a=(r^2-2s^2)/epsilon,
b=2rs/epsilon,
c=(r^2+2s^2)/epsilon,
with gcd(r,s)=1 and epsilon in {1,2} the frozen 2-primary primitive-content factor.


Then
boxed:
N_u=(r^4+4s^4)/epsilon^2=A_-*A_+,
where
A_-=[(r-s)^2+s^2]/epsilon,
A_+=[(r+s)^2+s^2]/epsilon,
and
boxed:
gcd(A_-,A_+)=1.


After the fixed (1+i)-normalization when epsilon=2, A_-,A_+ are primitive Gaussian norms
N(H_-),N(H_+)
with
boxed:
H_-*H_+=unit*(a+ib).


The common-u oriented fresh square conductor therefore splits uniquely:
boxed:
mathfrak M=mathfrak M_-*mathfrak M_+,
N(mathfrak M)=M_rel,
mathfrak M_-^2|H_-,
mathfrak M_+^2|H_+,
N(mathfrak M_-)*N(mathfrak M_+)=M_rel.


Because all fresh c_p vanish on this carrier, the quotient after removing each assigned square conductor is fresh-primitive at those primes.


D. Primitive-parameter lattice receiver.


After freezing epsilon and one oriented prime allocation, the two Gaussian square-divisibility conditions place primitive (r,s) in a rank-two lattice whose fresh index is
boxed:
M_rel^2
(up to the frozen 2-primary packet normalization).


For fixed M_rel, allocation/orientation multiplicity is M_rel^o(1).
Together with the already-audited fixed-u B^o(1) endpoint multiplicity, the exceptional carrier is reduced to
boxed:
B^o(1) unions of primitive determinant-M_rel^2 parameter lattices.


This is not itself a fixed-power count.


POPULATION:
Exact fixed-content/coefficient nondegenerate relative-fresh endpoint packet on the two singular fixed-x values from M3-T11-045.

x_E-14=(6*t)^2,


equivalently


Y_E^2=X^3-484*X^2+72900*X,
X-1134 is a rational square.


For t=a/b reduced, the three quadratic factors in the homogenized genus-two equation are pairwise coprime away from {2,3,5}; therefore each factor has squarefree kernel supported on {2,3,5}, giving a finite S-unit 2-descent.

## M3-T11-050

CLAIM:
On the x=27/40 genus-two receiver of M3-T11-047/048/049, both elliptic quotients have Mordell-Weil rank exactly one.


For the complementary quotient


E_2:
V^2=U*(U^2+1244*U+562500),


the standard 2-isogenous curve is


E_2':
y^2=x*(x+256)*(x-2744).


Exact primitive local-solubility elimination on the 2-isogeny homogeneous spaces gives


im(alpha_E2)={1,2}


and


im(alpha_E2')={1,-1,14,-14}.


The classical rational-2-torsion descent formula therefore gives


rank E_2(Q)=1.


For the first quotient

Y_E^2=X*(X^2-484*X+72900),

and the same exact local descent gives


im(alpha_E1)={1,2},

rank E_1(Q)=1.


The M3-T11-049 lift

is exactly equivalent for finite t to


U-2500=14*r^2,


r=25/(3*t).


Thus the live lift is the translated squareclass condition


[U-2500]=14.


Moreover, because im(alpha_E2)={1,2}, every rational E_2 point already has U-squareclass 1 or 2. The M3-T11-048 packet split is therefore exhaustive on E_2(Q) and is not an additional global restriction after passing to this quotient.


The two rational involutions of the genus-two curve induce a Q-isogeny


Jac(C) ~ E_1 x E_2,


so


rank Jac(C)(Q)=2.


Since genus(C)=2, the classical Chabauty-Coleman condition rank(J)<g fails exactly. Since the split product gives rho(J)>=2, the quadratic-Chabauty finiteness inequality


rank(J)<dim(J)+rho(J)-1


is satisfied.

[gamma_p]=res([A/(8*u)]).
So the entire local etale squareclass is determined by u/A.

The surviving cubic-resonant set is therefore exactly:
3|(2lambda+c_p) and the displayed residual cubic is reducible.

EXACT_RESOLVENT_ROOT_CURVE:
Set v=u^2. A rational root y of the cleared standard cubic resolvent lies on
F(v,y)=(v+1)^3*y^3+(-11*v^3-21*v^2-9*v+1)*y^2+4*v*(v-11)*(v+1)*y-4*v*(11*v^2+3*v+8)=0.

Disc_v(F)=-256*(y+1)*(27*y+28)^3.


NORMALIZATION:
v=-(t-2)*(t+1)^2/((t+4)*(t^2-4*t+13)).
y=-(t+1)*(2*t^2-11*t+23)/27.
Inverse away from the finite exceptional locus:
t=-2*(3*v*y+17*v+3*y+2)/(3*v*y-8*v+3*y+4).
On F the inverse denominator can vanish only at v=-1 or v=2/25; neither is a nonzero rational square.


SQUARE_PULLBACK:
For u!=0, with r=u/(t+1),
r^2=-(t-2)/((t+4)*(t^2-4*t+13)).
Equivalently
W^2=-(t-2)*(t+4)*(t^2-4*t+13).
With X=-6/(t-2), Y=2W/(t-2)^2, x=X-1 this is
E: Y^2=x*(x^2+2*x+5).


ELLIPTIC_DESCENT:
For E: Y^2=x^3+2*x^2+5*x, the 2-isogeny alpha image is {1,5}. The dual curve is Ebar: Y^2=x^3-4*x^2-16*x. Its possible extra squareclasses +/-2 would require
N^2=2*m^4-4*m^2*e^2-8*e^4
or
N^2=-2*m^4-4*m^2*e^2+8*e^4,
which are impossible mod 16 for primitive m,e in all parity cases. Thus the dual alpha image is {1,-1}, and the 2-isogeny rank formula gives rank E(Q)=0.
At p=3, #E(F_3)=2. The 3-division polynomial is (x+1)*(3*x^3+5*x^2+25*x-25); the cubic factor is irreducible over Q and x=-1 gives Y^2=-4. Hence E(Q) has no rational 3-torsion and E(Q)={O,(0,0)}.


BACK_SUBSTITUTION:
O maps to t=2 and v=0. The point (0,0) maps to t=-4, a pole of v(t). The canceled t=-1 also gives only v=0. Therefore no finite u in Q^* yields a rational resolvent root.

M3-T11-112 — Psi fixed-conductor primitive lattice counting adapter
STATUS=PROVISIONAL / EXACT_SAME_MEASURE_UPPER_BOUND / HOSTILE_AUDIT_REQUIRED / NO_FIXED_POWER_SAVING
TYPE=QUANTITATIVE_ADAPTER / PRIMITIVE_PARAMETER_COUNT / MOVING_MODULUS_FIREWALL
POPULATION=Exact nondegenerate physical Stage37 endpoints with R<=B in one fixed content/coefficient packet, restricted to psi/A4. One physical endpoint is one count.
DEPENDENCIES=111 HOSTILE_AUDIT_PASS; 109 exact degree-two psi parametrization; 040/041/043 capped common-u conductor; 036 HOSTILE_AUDIT_PASS uniform fixed-u physical multiplicity.
DUPLICATE_SEARCH=Compared RESULT-LEDGER, NEGATIVE-REGISTER, ROUTE and CARD-INDEX. Existing 029/030 fixed root-line occupancy and 046 primitive lattices are related engines; they do not give this psi depth pullback plus uniform primitive fixed-conductor bound. No prior saving or retired density route is reopened.
ALIASES=PsiA4PrimitiveFixedConductorCount; PsiDepthRootLineLatticeUpperBound.


STATEMENT.
Let M=M_rel, C=C_u with 0<=v_p(C)<=2v_p(M), and L=M^2 C. Fix M,C (hence L), and restrict physical points to those having at least one primitive psi parameter [r:s] with max(|r|,|s|)<=H, H>=1. Denote their number E_psi(B;M,C,H). Then
E_psi(B;M,C,H) << B^o(1) 4^omega(M) (H^2/L+1).
On the polynomial physical range, equivalently
E_psi(B;M,C,H) << B^o(1) (H^2/(M^2 C)+1).
The B^o(1) factor is the previously audited fixed-u physical multiplicity, not new multiplicity credit.
For a fixed oriented rho modulo L and one choice of the two psi root lines at every p, the primitive parameter count is O(H^2/L+1), with an absolute constant independent of lattice shape.


PROOF.
(i) Audited 111 gives p=1 mod12 at every p|M. Choose the existing common-u Gaussian root rho modulo L. At extreme c_p=2lambda, L uses only the capped depth 4lambda, which is valid even if the actual norm valuation is larger. No unjustified exact saturation is needed.
(ii) At each p^n||L the binary quadratic N-5rho Q0 has exactly two simple projective root lines. A line is the kernel of a primitive covector modulo p^n, including the infinity chart. Selecting one at every p and using CRT gives a primitive covector modulo L. Its kernel in Z^2 is a rank-two lattice Lambda of determinant exactly L: the covector map Z^2 -> Z/L is surjective.
(iii) Primitive lattice lemma. Choose a Gauss-reduced integral basis b1,b2 of Lambda, with |b1|<=|b2| and angle between 60 and 120 degrees. Then |b1||b2| is comparable to det(Lambda)=L. If v=m b1+n b2 has sup norm <=H, elementary inversion gives |m|<=K H/|b1| and |n|<=K H/|b2| for an absolute K. A Z^2-primitive v must have gcd(m,n)=1, since a common divisor divides both integer coordinates of v. For n=0 only m=+/-1 can survive. For n!=0, if such a vector occurs then both H/|b1| and H/|b2| are bounded below by an absolute positive constant. Thus the number is O((H/|b1|)(H/|b2|))=O(H^2/L). Adding the n=0 contribution proves O(H^2/L+1). This is a deterministic upper bound, including highly anisotropic lattices; there is no H/lambda1 error term.
(iv) There are at most 2^omega(M) Gaussian orientations and 2^omega(M) pullback line choices, hence at most 4^omega(M) lattices. Sum their upper bounds. Counting signed primitive pairs overcounts projective parameters by only a bounded factor.
(v) Every counted physical endpoint has a parameter in this set. Each parameter determines exactly one u=psi(r/s); apply audited 036 to bound physical multiplicity for each realized u by B^o(1). Extra endpoint equations and exact R<=B restrictions are monotone post-filters. No ambient density is substituted for the physical population.


HEIGHT AND MOVING-CONDUCTOR CONSEQUENCE.
H is a stated parameter-height cutoff, not an asserted power of B. The exact psi height relation is h(u)=2h(t)+O(1) for logarithmic heights, but no new sharp physical B-exponent is proved here.
For finitely many fixed conductor pairs (M,C) in a shell, with a common valid cutoff H, the rigorous union upper bound is
B^o(1) sum_(M,C) (H^2/(M^2 C)+1).
Duplicates only enlarge this upper bound.
To bound active realized u-values below B^(1/12-delta), it is sufficient to establish that this actual physical-shell sum is O(B^(1/12-delta)), or to replace the separate-modulus sum by a sharper joint incidence bound. Such an estimate is NOT proved.
The +1 term records the thin-lattice / large-modulus occupancy obstruction: when L>H^2, this method gives O(B^o(1)) per conductor pair rather than a reciprocal-L gain that can be summed freely. No physical lower-bound or actual endpoint existence is asserted by this observation.


IMPLIES=The psi fixed-conductor counting adapter is quantitative, but moving-conductor occupancy and a sharp physical height relation remain the blockers.
DO_NOT_REPEAT=Do not multiply p=1 mod12 density, two-line density, common-u root-line charge or determinant probabilities. The displayed estimate replaces a count; it is not an independent factor in a previously obtained numerator bound. Do not delete +1, assume independence, or turn ambient psi height into a physical B-exponent.

M3-T11-113 — Psi norm-squareclass twist compression and joint large-conductor tail
STATUS=PROVISIONAL / HOSTILE_AUDIT_REQUIRED / EXACT_SAME_MEASURE_THEOREM_ADAPTER
TYPE=FIXED_SQUARECLASS_UNIFORM_FIBER / MOVING_CONDUCTOR_JOINT_TAIL / HEIGHT_WINDOW_POWER_BOUND
POPULATION=Exact nondegenerate Stage37 physical endpoints with R<=B in one fixed content/coefficient packet, restricted to the audited psi/A4 image. One endpoint is one count.
DEPENDENCIES=109 psi parametrization; corrected 111; audited 112; 035/040/041 exact common-u conductor; 036 audited fixed-u physical multiplicity and polynomial physical coordinate-height machinery; Dujella Theorem 1.1.
DUPLICATE_SEARCH=RESULT-LEDGER, NEGATIVE-REGISTER, active ROUTE and CARD-INDEX were compared. The earlier genus-2 fixed-squareclass variable d in 101..107 is sf(2Pi), not the variable below. This card fixes sf(a^2+b^2) only on psi, using a new fixed norm quartic. It does not reopen local S4 squareclass work or ordinary fixed-theta Kummer.
ALIASES=PsiCommonUNormSquareclassTwistCompression; PsiJointLargeMConductorTail; PsiLowParameterHeightOneTwelfthWindow.
DUPLICATE_OF=NONE.


1. Exact norm and reduction.
Write primitive psi parameter t=r/s and
N=r^2-2rs-s^2, Q0=r^2+s^2, u=N/(5Q0).
Define
F(r,s)=N^2+25Q0^2
=26r^4-4r^3s+52r^2s^2+4rs^3+26s^4.
IMPORTANT_COEFFICIENT=52, not 48.
For primitive (r,s), g=gcd(N,5Q0) is exactly 1 or 2. Odd common divisors of N,Q0 are excluded by the resultant 8s^4; N has no primitive zero mod5. For mixed parity g=1; for both odd N,Q0 each have valuation exactly 1 at 2, so g=2.
Thus reduced u=a/b has
a^2+b^2=F(r,s)/g^2.
The canonical positive squarefree kernel
d=sf(a^2+b^2)=sf(F(r,s))
is independent of the parameter preimage: g^2 and projective scaling are squares.
For H=max(|r|,|s|), |N|<=4H^2 and Q0<=2H^2, hence
0<F(r,s)<=116H^4.
This is a direct height inequality; no physical B-exponent for H is imported.


2. New fixed-d genus-one fiber.
For a positive squarefree d, write F(r,s)=d q^2. Then the parameter point lies on the smooth genus-one double cover
C_d: Y^2=d F(t,1),
with Y=d q/s^2 on the finite chart, and the projective infinity chart retained.
For the binary quartic F, using the same scaled-Jacobian convention as 036:
I=10864,
J=2219776,
4I^3-J^2=201553920000 !=0.
For dF the invariants are I_d=d^2 I, J_d=d^3 J. Therefore
E_d: y^2=x^3-293328d^2 x-59933952d^3
=(x-624d)(x+276d)(x+348d).
For every d>0 the three roots are distinct. Consequently E_d has full rational 2-torsion over Q; in particular (624d,0) has exact order 2.
This family is a rational quadratic-twist family of one fixed elliptic curve, not the old fixed-u or fixed-theta family.


3. Uniform fixed-d parameter and physical count.
Assume H<=B^A for one fixed A, as allowed by the audited polynomial physical range. For realized d, d<=116H^4<=B^O_A(1).
The standard degree-four binary-quartic 2-cover C_d -> Jac(C_d)=E_d, used as a counting interface in 036, has fixed-degree algebraic formulas whose coefficient heights grow polynomially in d. Thus a parameter point of height <=H and Y=d q/s^2 maps to an E_d(Q) point of naive x-height B^O_A(1). Branch/pole/infinity charts contribute only bounded exceptional points.
The model height h(E_d)=O(log d)=O_A(log B).
The canonical-height comparison quoted in Dujella's paper gives canonical height O_A(log B). Choose a single enlarged height parameter T=B^K_A, with K_A fixed and large enough both for the induced point bound and T>=exp(max(h(E_d),e)).
Dujella Theorem 1.1 applies over the fixed field Q with prime order 2:
# such E_d(Q) points <=exp(O_A(log B/log log B))=B^o(1),
uniformly for every realized d.
The covering degree is four, so fixed d gives B^o(1) primitive projective psi parameters in the physical polynomial-height range. Composing each parameter t -> u with audited 036 gives B^o(1) physical endpoints for fixed d and fixed packet. Two subpolynomial bounds multiply to a subpolynomial bound; they are not charged as separate density savings.


4. Joint large-conductor tail — no per-modulus +1 sum.
Let E_psi(B;H,M0) count those exact physical endpoints admitting a primitive psi parameter of height <=H and with their actual M_rel>=M0>=1.
The audited common-u conductor gives M_rel^2 | a^2+b^2, hence M_rel^2 | F(r,s).
Removing the square factor M_rel^2 preserves d and leaves a positive integer, so
d=sf(F/M_rel^2)<=F/M_rel^2<=116H^4/M0^2.
Therefore every endpoint is routed once by its canonical d to one of at most
D=floor(116H^4/M0^2)
positive squarefree integer values.
Applying (3) to each d gives the provisional same-measure upper bound
E_psi(B;H,M0) <<_A B^o(1) H^4/M0^2.
If D=0 the subset is empty. The elementary ambient parameter upper bound plus 036 also gives B^o(1)H^2; hence
E_psi(B;H,M0) <<_A B^o(1) min(H^2,H^4/M0^2).
This sums over all moving actual M_rel and C_u simultaneously. It does not sum 112's +1 over conductor pairs, and it does not assume any distribution or independence of d.
The incremental C_u is not charged; only the already-existing square M_rel^2 is used as a deterministic divisor in a replacement count.


5. Precisely scoped exponent consequence.
On a height/conductor window H<=B^h and M_rel>=B^m, the new bound is
E_psi << B^(4h-2m+o(1)).
Thus a one-twelfth support deficit is obtained for this psi subpopulation if
4h-2m<1/12.
For the hard conductor threshold m=1/12-eta, it is sufficient to have
h<1/16-eta/2.
For example H<=B^(1/16-epsilon), M_rel>=B^(1/12-eta), with 4epsilon>2eta, gives
E_psi << B^(1/12-4epsilon+2eta+o(1)).
This is a bounded-height-window result only. No claim is made that all physical psi endpoints satisfy this small parameter-height bound. The remaining high-height psi region is uncontrolled by this one-twelfth argument.
No primary-gate closure, total numerator improvement or P/M3 limit is claimed.

The source supplies the uniform torsion counting theorem only; all norm/Jacobian/physical adapters here are newly derived and provisional.

M3-T11-114 — Psi incremental-conductor squarepart tail and parity-sensitive height window
STATUS=PROVISIONAL / HOSTILE_AUDIT_REQUIRED / EXACT_SAME_MEASURE_UPPER_BOUND
TYPE=INCREMENTAL_CONDUCTOR_ADAPTER / JOINT_SQUARECLASS_TAIL / PARITY_SENSITIVE_HEIGHT_WINDOW
POPULATION=Exact nondegenerate Stage37 physical endpoints with R<=B in one fixed content/coefficient packet, restricted to psi/A4; one endpoint is one count.
DEPENDENCIES=113 HOSTILE_AUDIT_PASS; 040/041/043 capped conductor; corrected 111; 036 uniform fixed-u multiplicity.
ALIASES=PsiIncrementalConductorSquarepartTail; PsiConductorParityHeightWindow.
DUPLICATE_SEARCH=RESULT-LEDGER, active ROUTE, NEGATIVE-REGISTER and CARD-INDEX checked for squarepart/parity/conductor variants. 112 is a fixed-modulus lattice count; 113 used M_rel^2 only and explicitly left C_u uncharged. Older squarefree kernels belong to different populations or equations. This result newly routes the incremental C_u squarepart into the joint norm-squareclass count.
DUPLICATE_OF=NONE.


1. Exact parity-safe square divisor.
Let M=M_rel and C=C_u. The accepted divisibility is
M^2*C | N_u=a^2+b^2,
with 0<=c_p=v_p(C)<=2lambda_p for every p^lambda_p||M.
Write uniquely C=kappa*T^2, where kappa=sf(C) is squarefree and
T=product_(p|M) p^floor(c_p/2).
Define S_sq=M*T. This symbol is NOT the existing symmetric coordinate S.
Then exactly
S_sq^2=M^2*C/kappa | N_u,
M<=S_sq<=M^2.
Only divisibility is used. The formula remains valid at capped extreme depth even if actual norm valuations exceed the cap. No old exact-saturation assertion is imported.
For psi, N_u=F(r,s)/g^2, g in {1,2}, so S_sq^2|F as well.


2. Joint actual-conductor upper bound.
Let E_psi(B;H,S0) count the physical subset admitting a primitive psi parameter of height<=H and whose actual S_sq>=S0>=1.
The canonical d=sf(N_u)=sf(F) satisfies
d=sf(N_u/S_sq^2)<=N_u/S_sq^2<=116H^4/S0^2.
Audited 113 gives B^o(1) physical endpoints uniformly per d; sum over canonical d only, simultaneously over all M,C.
Thus for H<=B^A,
E_psi(B;H,S0)<<_A B^o(1)min(H^2,H^4/S0^2).
If floor(116H^4/S0^2)=0 the subset is empty.
In a shell M>=M0, C>=C0, kappa<=K0, every endpoint has S_sq^2>=M0^2*C0/K0, hence
E_psi<<_A B^o(1)min(H^2,H^4*K0/(M0^2*C0)).
K0>=1. No sum over conductor pairs or kappa values is needed. This is one replacement count, not 113 multiplied by a new independent probability.


3. Exponent window and gain over 113.
If H<=B^h, M>=B^m, C>=B^c, kappa<=B^k, then
E_psi<<B^(4h-2m-c+k+o(1)).
It beats one-twelfth on this subset if
4h-2m-c+k<1/12.
On the extreme amplified allocation C=M^2, kappa=1 and S_sq=M^2. Therefore the joint upper bound over all M>=B^m is
E_psi<<B^(4h-4m+o(1)),
and suffices when h<m+1/48.
For m=1/12-eta this allows h<5/48-eta, compared with 113's h<1/16-eta/2.
Example: H<=B^(5/48-epsilon), M>=B^(1/12-eta), C=M^2, epsilon>eta implies
E_psi<<B^(1/12-4epsilon+4eta+o(1)).
This includes a wider height window on this allocation, but no assertion that all physical psi endpoints lie in it or in the extreme allocation.


4. Parity obstruction and precise remaining receiver.
One cannot replace S_sq^2 by M^2*C unless C is a square. Odd c_p leaves p in kappa. Example lambda=1,c_p=1 gives C=p, kappa=p and S_sq=M: no new square divisor is extracted.
A large C alone therefore supplies no polynomial improvement if kappa is comparably large.
For a dyadic parameter shell H~B^h, a sufficient low-occupancy condition is
S_sq>=B^(2h-1/24+epsilon),
giving E_psi<<B^(1/12-2epsilon+o(1)).
The still-uncontrolled physical subset is high parameter height with small S_sq relative to this threshold. Within the amplified-u branch C>=M, this includes high odd-valuation kernel kappa, not just large C.
The old complementary identity Q_S*C=M^2 remains available; no distribution/correlation theorem for kappa, Q_S, H or actual endpoints is proved here.


5. Supporting checks and firewall.
48 valuation profiles lambda=1..6, c=0..2lambda, with three actual norm depths at or above the guaranteed depth, verified S_sq^2=M^2*C/kappa, divisibility and sf(norm)<=norm/S_sq^2.
The exact proof is the displayed primewise floor formula and audited 113 routing; finite tests are supporting only.
IMPLIES=Incremental C_u can strengthen the joint psi bound only through its squarepart. A larger scoped height window exists on C=M^2; high-height/low-squarepart occupancy remains the blocker.

M3-T11-115 — Psi core-supported norm squareclass compression without a small parameter-height cutoff
STATUS=PROVISIONAL / HOSTILE_AUDIT_REQUIRED / EXACT_SAME_MEASURE_SUPPORT_ADAPTER
TYPE=GLOBAL_CORE_SUPPORT_LOCALIZATION / FIXED_SUPPORT_UNIFORM_FIBER / HEIGHT_FREE_SUPPORT_WINDOW
POPULATION=Exact nondegenerate Stage37 physical endpoints with R<=B in one fixed content/coefficient packet, restricted to psi/A4. One endpoint is one count.
DEPENDENCIES=113 HOSTILE_AUDIT_PASS; audited 114; corrected 111; 036 polynomial physical heights; corrected three-anti-root denominator carriers (ROUTE section 32); 033 fixed-content support; the integer-normal-form M3-T11-042 entry, explicitly identified by N_u/g_u|D (not the other historical 042 entry).
ALIASES=PsiCoreSupportedNormSquareclassCompression; PsiCommonCoreRadicalTimesActualRelativeOddKernel.
DUPLICATE_SEARCH=MAIN/INDEX/RESULT-LEDGER/ROUTE/NEGATIVE-REGISTER and CARD-INDEX checked for d_rel, core radical and norm-support variants. 084/085 localized the residual kernel on the retired x=-1/8 carrier, where relative norm valuations are even. This result instead treats the live psi/A4 population, retains its actual relative odd kernel, and uses 113's new fixed norm-quartic fibers. 113/114 only bounded d by parameter height divided by a square divisor. This result counts core-supported d without a small-H cutoff.
DUPLICATE_OF=NONE.


1. Retained support carrier and explicit packet primes.
Write the corrected anti-roots v_i=A_i/B_i reduced, D=B_1*B_2*B_3 and R_rel=tau_1*tau_2*tau_3.
The valid complementary carriers are
B_1 | L_1*(tau_0*tau_2*tau_3)^2,
B_2 | L_2*(tau_0*tau_1*tau_3)^2,
B_3 | L_3*(tau_0*tau_1*tau_2)^2,
where each L_i is a positive fixed-packet factor in the retained polynomial range.
Multiplying gives
D | L_1*L_2*L_3*tau_0^6*R_rel^4.
For the canonical reduced u=a/b, N_u=a^2+b^2 and g_u=gcd(4,N_u) in {1,2}, the integer-normal-form identity gives
N_u/g_u | D.
Consequently
N_u | 2*L_1*L_2*L_3*tau_0^6*R_rel^4.
Only support containment is needed. No false same-v CRT from old section 31 is used.


Let P_pkt=2*L_1*L_2*L_3*c_1*c_2*c_3 and Delta_pkt=rad(P_pkt).
Keep these packet primes explicitly: L_i may contain coefficient primes outside the content-prime set.
P_pkt is fixed within the packet and <=B^K for one fixed retained K, so
2^omega(P_pkt)=B^o(1).
This follows from the primorial/factorial lower bound, uniformly over the allowed polynomial packets.


2. Actual relative odd kernel, not a capped proxy.
Let d=sf(N_u) be 113's canonical positive norm squareclass.
Define
d_rel=gcd(d,rad(M_rel))
=product_(p|M_rel, v_p(N_u) odd) p.
Set R0=rad(tau_0^sharp), with tau_0^sharp the part of tau_0 outside the content-prime set, and
Xi=R0*d_rel.
Xi is a positive integer in the polynomial physical range; it is not an independent random coordinate.
All primes of R_rel/M_rel lie in the content-prime set. Thus if p|d but p does not divide Delta_pkt*M_rel, the support carrier in (1) forces p|tau_0^sharp. Since d is squarefree,
d | Delta_pkt*R0*d_rel = Delta_pkt*Xi.


3. Uniform fixed-Xi physical count; all physical parameter heights included.
For any fixed Xi, at most 2^omega(Delta_pkt*Xi)=B^o(1) squarefree values d divide Delta_pkt*Xi.
Audited 113 gives B^o(1) physical psi endpoints per d, uniformly on the retained polynomial physical-height range. Hence
# physical psi endpoints compatible with fixed Xi << B^o(1).
No count of M_rel,C_u, anti-root triples, parameter heights or Gaussian orientations is multiplied into this estimate. They are all absorbed within the canonical fixed-d physical fiber.
Every physical psi point has a polynomial parameter-height bound: reduced psi denominator is b=5(r^2+s^2)/g with g in {1,2}, so H(t)^2<=r^2+s^2=g*b/5<=2b/5. Polynomial physical height of u from 036 therefore places its primitive psi preimages in 113's allowed polynomial range. No H<=B^(1/16) or other small exponent is assumed.


Let E_psi(B;Xi<=Z) count physical endpoints admitting a retained core representation with Xi<=Z, Z>=1 polynomially bounded. Then
E_psi(B;Xi<=Z)<<B^o(1)*Z.
If a core representation is not unique, the union over integer Xi values is still an upper bound and endpoints remain counted once. No injectivity of Xi is needed.
In particular Xi<=B^(1/12-delta) gives
E_psi<<B^(1/12-delta+o(1))
with no small parameter-height cutoff.
More generally any allowed Xi support set of cardinality A(B) gives A(B)*B^o(1).


4. Connection to 114 and the extreme-depth guard.
At p^lambda||M_rel, corrected 111 gives min(v_p(N_u),4lambda)=2lambda+c_p.
For c_p<2lambda, actual parity equals c_p mod2.
For c_p=2lambda, actual valuation may exceed 4lambda; its excess parity must be retained.
Define
e_ext=product_(p|M_rel, c_p=2lambda_p, v_p(N_u) odd) p.
Then with kappa=sf(C_u),
d_rel=kappa*e_ext.
Their supports are disjoint, because extreme capped c_p is even.
Thus the new receiver is explicitly
Xi=rad(tau_0^sharp)*sf(C_u)*e_ext.
Do not silently set e_ext=1 from capped data. Even C_u=M_rel^2 only implies kappa=1; actual even norm valuation is an additional condition for d_rel=1.


For the actual-even relative stratum d_rel=1, the subset R0<=B^(1/12-delta) is small at the same physical one-twelfth scale for every physical parameter height.
For general d_rel, a sufficient window is R0<=B^a and d_rel<=B^b with a+b<1/12.
On an intersection also satisfying 114's H,S0 cutoffs one may take the minimum of valid upper bounds:
E_psi<<B^o(1)*min(Z,H^2,H^4/S0^2).
This is a minimum of replacement counts, not a product of savings.


5. What remains unresolved.
The result does not prove that every psi endpoint has small Xi, or that the occupied Xi support has cardinality below B^(1/12).
Large Xi can arise from a large all-same core radical, a large actual relative odd kernel, or both. Such large support is the new minimal global occurrence/correlation receiver.
Some high-H/low-S_sq points are now controlled if Xi is small; no claim is made that all such points are controlled.
The fixed Xi fiber bound does not itself constrain how many Xi values occur. Bounding occupied Xi cardinality is necessary before claiming total psi support saving.
The local S4 tuple remains frozen, x=-1/8 stays retired, and phi/nonlocal S4/theta!=0 remain live.

# M3-T11-116 — complementary norm-cofactor fibers and a height-free two-sided window


STATUS=PROVISIONAL / HOSTILE_AUDIT_REQUIRED / EXACT_SAME_MEASURE_UPPER_BOUND
TYPE=COMPLEMENTARY_NORM_COFACTOR / JOINT_MOVING_CORE_COUNT / TWO_SIDED_SUPPORT_WINDOW
POPULATION=Exact nondegenerate physical Stage37 psi/A4 endpoints with R<=B in one fixed content/coefficient packet; one endpoint is one count.
DEPENDENCIES=Audited 113, 114, 115; corrected denominator carriers; integer-normal-form N_u/g_u|D; polynomial physical range from 036.
ALIASES=PsiComplementaryNormCofactor; PsiTwoSidedNormSquarepartWindow.
DUPLICATE_SEARCH=Current MAIN/INDEX/RESULT-LEDGER/active ROUTE checked for norm quotient/cofactor and complementary squareclass variants. Older theta cofactors and elliptic/genus-2 quotients concern different equations/populations. 113/114 count small norm squareclasses; 115 counts small core support. None uses the integer quotient of the live psi norm into its even-power core carrier. DUPLICATE_OF=NONE.


## 1. Integral cofactor with fixed-packet squareclass


Let L=L1*L2*L3, Rrel=tau1*tau2*tau3, and define


W_car=2*L*tau0^6*Rrel^4,
J_car=W_car/N_u.


Audited 115 gives N_u | W_car, so J_car is a positive integer. This symbol J_car is unrelated to the binary-quartic invariant J=2219776. W_car is not the actual reduced denominator D: it is an upper divisibility carrier. No equality D=W_car is assumed.


The core contribution tau0^6*Rrel^4 is a square. From N_u*J_car=W_car it follows exactly that


d=sf(N_u)=sf(2*L*J_car).


Thus for fixed J_car and the fixed packet, d is uniquely determined. Audited 113 gives B^o(1) physical psi endpoints for that d. This absorbs all moving core choices, conductor allocations, orientations and parameter heights; none is charged again. If endpoints admit several retained core representations, union counting remains valid.


For Y>=1 in the polynomial physical range,


E_psi(B; J_car<=Y) << B^o(1)*Y.


More generally an allowed J_car support set of cardinality A gives A B^o(1). This receiver applies to large-Xi endpoints as well: no condition on rad(tau0^sharp)*d_rel is imposed. It does not prove J_car small globally.


## 2. A high-parameter-height window


Write the primitive psi parameter t=r/s and H=max(|r|,|s|). Audited reduction gives N_u=F(r,s)/g^2, g in {1,2}, where


F=(r^2-2rs-s^2)^2+25(r^2+s^2)^2 >=25 H^4.


Therefore N_u >=(25/4)H^4. On any exact physical subset with H>=H0, tau0<=T0 and Rrel<=U0 (U0 is a magnitude bound, not 115's common-core radical R0),


J_car <=(8/25)*L*T0^6*U0^4/H0^4,
E_psi << B^o(1)*floor((8/25)*L*T0^6*U0^4/H0^4).


If the floor is zero this subset is empty. L is fixed in the packet; it may grow polynomially with B and must not be silently treated as an absolute constant. With L<=B^ell, T0<=B^t, U0<=B^r, H0>=B^h, a sufficient one-twelfth window is


ell+6t+4r-4h <1/12.


This complements the low-H windows of 113/114. It is a scoped bound, not a proof that all physical parameter heights are high enough relative to their cores.


## 3. Height-free two-sided covering criterion


Retain 114's S_sq=M_rel*T with C_u=kappa*T^2 and kappa=sf(C_u). Then S_sq^2 | N_u and S_sq^2 | W_car. Define


V_norm=N_u/S_sq^2,
K_car=W_car/S_sq^2.


Both are positive integers, and exactly


d=sf(V_norm),
V_norm*J_car=K_car.


For Z,Y>=1, endpoints admitting a representation with K_car<=Z*Y satisfy V_norm<=Z or J_car<=Y. If both strict inequalities failed, their product would exceed Z*Y. The first subset has d<=Z and the second has at most floor(Y) cofactor values. Therefore


E_psi(B; K_car<=Z*Y) << B^o(1)*(floor(Z)+floor(Y)).


In particular, for polynomial K0>=1,


E_psi(B; K_car<=K0) << B^o(1)*sqrt(K0),


by choosing Z=Y=sqrt(K0). Hence K_car<=B^(1/6-2delta), delta>0, gives a one-twelfth support deficit B^(1/12-delta+o(1)) without any small-H cutoff. This is a union of two replacement counts; no independence is assumed.


Explicitly


K_car=2*L*tau0^6*Rrel^4*kappa/(M_rel^2*C_u).


Do not infer that a large C_u alone makes K_car small: the actual kappa and all common/nonfresh core factors remain. Because S_sq<=M_rel^2<=Rrel^2, K_car>=2*L*tau0^6. Thus this balanced window cannot automatically cover large common-core magnitude. The direct small-J_car window is more general than the balanced criterion.


## 4. Exact residual receiver and audit plan


For chosen Z_Xi,Z,Y, the union of Xi<=Z_Xi, V_norm<=Z and J_car<=Y has count <<B^o(1)*(Z_Xi+Z+Y). The unresolved complement has simultaneously Xi>Z_Xi, V_norm>Z and J_car>Y, and therefore K_car>ZY. This is a receiver definition, not a distribution theorem. It replaces the overly exclusive requirement to control large Xi by Xi cardinality alone.

## 1. First invalid inference


M3-T11-106 says the physical evaluation coordinate is z_phys=S/2. M3-T11-109/110 says that on the phi image the polynomial Q_u has a unique rational root vartheta=N/Q0. A rational evaluation point is not thereby a root. These two rational objects cannot be identified merely from the uniqueness of the polynomial's rational root.


The previously audited M3-T11-110 explicitly states: do not identify vartheta with physical z=S/2; vartheta is a root, whereas z is the evaluation point in the etale descent. M3-T11-105 gives the physical condition Q_u(z)/A=-w^2, not Q_u(z)=0.


Thus the opening root lock S=2N/Q0 in M3-T11-120 has no valid physical adapter. Substituting it in later algebra does not establish it on physical endpoints.


## 2. Exact discriminant certificate


Put A=1+u^2 and retain the actual symmetric cubic


f(X)=X^3-S*X^2+E*X-Pi,
E=4u(S-u)/A,
Pi=4u^2*S/A.


The standard cubic discriminant is


Delta=S^2*E^2-4E^3-4S^3*Pi-27Pi^2+18S*E*Pi.


Direct expansion gives the polynomial identity


A^3*Delta/(16u^2)
=A*S^2*(S-u)^2-16u*(S-u)^3-A^2*S^4-27u^2*A*S^2+18u*A*S^2*(S-u)
=-u^2*(A*S^4-16u*S^3+(44u^2-4)*S^2+48u*S-16u^2).


Since the last parenthesis is 16Q_u(S/2), exactly


Delta=-256u^4*Q_u(S/2)/A^3.


For the retained distinct rational anti-roots v_i, let D_diff=product_(i<j)(v_i-v_j). Then Delta=D_diff^2, and


Q_u(z_phys)/A=-(A*D_diff/(16u^2))^2.


On the nonzero-discriminant locus this is a nonzero negative rational square. In particular z_phys is not any root of Q_u, including vartheta. If one forcibly sets z_phys=vartheta, Delta=0 and the symmetric cubic has repeated roots: this is the branch/degenerate locus, not the distinct-root physical adapter used in the retained descent.


This does NOT prove the whole physical phi population empty. The condition z_phys=vartheta was never proved for that population, so contradiction after imposing it cannot eliminate phi.
