## Authority and correction
Continue freshly fetched MAIN/INDEX/RESULT-LEDGER/active ROUTE139 and latest139 card; targeted138 parity/height,134 signed eliminant, old ROUTE41 nonzero S/P, and all-same/core interfaces17/28/32. No full-history reread. Original exact primitive physical R, positive edges, canonical signed face witness, content/coefficient/orientation/cyclic masks and one endpoint one count remain.


CORRECTION TO139 CONTINUATION: its generic zero-Heron polynomial discussion is algebraically correct, but its proposed physical C_A=0 / M_rel=1 research branch is EMPTY by parity, even when relative fresh support is empty. The example (3,4,5) has an even coordinate and is not a physical plus-vector. Retain139 polynomial, signed divisor and exact lift; retire only that unnecessary physical zero-carrier continuation. This does not exclude all M_rel=1 endpoints.


## 1. Uniform nonzero factors, no fresh hypothesis
From138, A_i=e_i+f_i are all odd and primitive. Set F_0=sum A_i^2, F_i=F_0-2A_i^2.
Odd squares are1 mod8. Thus
 F_0=3 mod8, F_i=1 mod8 for i=1,2,3.
All four factors are nonzero, and C_A=-product F_j=5 mod8 is nonzero. This holds for all primitive physical signed witnesses, all contents and all charts; no finite-u/fresh theorem is needed.139's square-divisor enumeration is therefore finite throughout the physical population.


## 2. Positive physical directions have S and all v_i nonzero
Use d_i=2x_i y_i, S=sum d_i, v_i=S-2d_i, sum x_i^2=1, x_i^2+y_i^2=1. Positive three edges ensure each x_i>0 and each y_i!=0, hence each d_i!=0.
The134 actual signed-sphere identity gives
 T(v)=(SE+P)^2-S^2 P(4S-P)=0,
 E=sum_(i<j)v_i v_j, P=product v_i.
If S=0, then T=P^2 forces P=0, but v_i=-2d_i are all nonzero: contradiction.
If v_i=0, then P=0 and T=(SE)^2. Since S!=0, E=0. Writing the other roots v_j,v_k gives E=v_j v_k=0. Hence a second root vanishes. The remaining root equals S, giving d_k=(S-v_k)/2=0 for its index, again a contradiction.
Nonzero S on the old nondegenerate branch was already retained in ROUTE41; do not credit it as a new counting theorem. This direct physical proof explains why positivity is essential and permits the next elementary integer exclusion without a new u chart assumption.


## 3. No single Heron factor absorbs the whole squared physical diagonal
Directly, F_0/R^2=3+S and F_i/R^2=1+v_i.
Cauchy gives |S|<=2sqrt(2), so
 0<3-2sqrt(2)<=F_0/R^2<=3+2sqrt(2)<6.
If R^2|F_0, its integer quotient is between0 and6 and is3 mod8, because R is odd and R^2=1 mod8. Thus the quotient is3, forcing S=0, impossible.


Each A_i^2 lies in(0,2R^2], so -2<F_i/R^2<4 (the weaker closed bounds also suffice). If R^2|F_i, its integer quotient in[-2,4] is1 mod8, hence1. This forces v_i=0, impossible.
Therefore
 R^2 does NOT divide F_j for any j=0,1,2,3,
although139 proves R^2 divides their product.
This is an exact same-R set exclusion, not a character probability or a support power bound. It applies to every primitive positive endpoint and each signed face witness. Boundary points with a zero edge can violate full-factor exclusion; they are excluded from this theorem.


Equivalently each gcd(R^2,|F_j|) is a proper divisor of R^2. Do not infer a fixed power gap from properness: the missing prime-power can be bounded while R grows. No uniform R^epsilon split has been proved.


## 4. Noncontent support has a unique four-factor square allocation
Let H_c=h_1 h_2 h_3, h_i=gcd(e_i,R), using the retained pairwise-coprime content interface. Define
 R_nc=product_(p^lambda||R, p not dividing H_c) p^lambda.
This removes FULL prime powers supported by H_c, not just a numerical quotient R/H_c.
For each such odd prime, gcd(A_i,R)=h_i implies every A_i is a p-unit. At most one of the four F_j can be divisible by p: a pair F_0,F_i differs by2A_i^2; a pair F_i,F_j sums to2A_k^2 for the third index. These are p-units.139's R^2|product F_j forces exactly one factor to have valuation at least2lambda.
Color the prime by that unique factor j and let n_j be the product of its FULL p^lambda powers. Then
 pairwise gcd(n_j,n_k)=1, product_(j=0..3)n_j=R_nc, n_j^2|F_j.
This is a global integer router for all noncontent support, including support outside the relative-fresh m_i. It does not assume every noncontent prime is relative fresh.


In particular if H_c=1, then R_nc=R; a single nontrivial n_j=R would contradict Section3. Every physical endpoint in this content-free case must therefore have at least two nontrivial factor colors. For general contents, do NOT assert this from R_nc alone: primes removed by H_c can provide the missing whole-R square allocation. Relative-fresh139 exact depth and target label remain valid, not independent new density.


Interpretation by local face signs: since each e_i is a unit, f_i/e_i is a square root of-1 modp^(2lambda), hence p=1 mod4. Pick either local root iota. If all three ratios equal the same sign of iota, the unique factor is F_0; if one index i has the opposite sign, the factor is F_i. This follows from A_i^2=2(sign_i)iota e_i^2 modp^(2lambda) and sum e_i^2=0 there. Switching iota reverses all signs and preserves the color. This is a physical pullback of existing common/relative orientation, not permission to identify n_0 with an old Gaussian core without its content/coefficient adapter.

# M3-T11-141 — Content-complete Heron square allocation on exact tau


STATUS=PROVED_PAIR_CONTENT_GCD_ADAPTER_AND_FULL_TAU_FOUR_FACTOR_COVER
AUDIT_MODE=WITHIN_SESSION_ADVERSARIAL_REDERIVATION_NOT_EXTERNAL
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0
PRIMARY_GATE_STATUS=OPEN
TI=PARKED
NEXT=M3-T11-142 ContentCompleteHeronLargeSquareDivisorRealizedSupport


## Authority and physical scope
Fresh MAIN/INDEX/RESULT-LEDGER/active ROUTE140 and latest140; targeted139 integer signed lift,138 primitive plus-vector and134 denominator/content interface. Targeted Heron/gcd lookup found no earlier content-complete adapter. Known full history not reread. Retain exact primitive positive physical endpoint R<=B, canonical ordered signed face witness, original content/coefficient/orientation/parity/cyclic masks and one endpoint one count.140 parity-empty zero factors and no single full-R-square factor remain;139 exact monic cover and signed R^2 divisor retained.120 remains retracted.


Notation: A_i=e_i+f_i (physical integer PLUS vector), h_i=gcd(A_i,R)=gcd(e_i,R), H_c=h_1 h_2 h_3, tau=R/H_c. These h_i are pairwise coprime and H_c|R by134. Define F_0=sum A_i^2 and F_i=F_0-2A_i^2. All F are odd and nonzero by140, and R^2|product F by139. New q_j below are allocation divisors, NOT physical hypotenuses D_i or historical anti-root denominators.


## 1. Every pairwise overlap on R is bounded by its exact content
For distinct i,j,k in{1,2,3},
 F_0-F_i=2A_i^2, F_j+F_k=2A_i^2.
Because the F factors are odd,
 gcd(F_0,F_i,R^2) divides h_i^2,
 gcd(F_j,F_k,R^2) divides h_i^2.
Absolute values are used in integer gcds. Indeed an odd common divisor divides A_i^2, and gcd(A_i^2,R^2)=h_i^2. These are exact divisor bounds, uniform across packets, with contents explicitly present.


Also gcd of ANY THREE distinct F factors equals1. An odd prime dividing F_0,F_i,F_j would divide A_i,A_j and then the remaining A_k via F_0; a prime dividing F_1,F_2,F_3 would divide every A_i from the pair sums. This contradicts primitive gcd(A)=1. The prime2 divides no F.


## 2. Canonical allocation of ALL tau, including content-supported powers
Fix p^lambda||R and put kappa=v_p(H_c). At most one h_i has positive p-adic depth, and kappa<=lambda. Let d_j=v_p(F_j), j=0..3, using finite valuations because F_j!=0. Triple gcd1 implies at most two positive d_j, and139 gives sum d_j>=2lambda.


If kappa=0, Section1 makes the positive factor unique and its depth at least2lambda.
If kappa>0 and two factors have positive depth, their minimum depth is at most2kappa by Section1. Therefore their maximum depth is at least2lambda-2kappa. If just one factor is positive, its depth is at least2lambda and the same bound holds.
Consequently, for every prime with lambda>kappa, choose the factor j having maximal d_j, breaking ties by smallest index, and allocate p^(lambda-kappa) to q_j.
Then the q_j are uniquely defined by the actual A,R and
 pairwise gcd(q_j,q_k)=1,
 product_(j=0..3)q_j=tau,
 q_j^2|F_j for each j.
This replaces140's router on R_nc (which removed COMPLETE content-supported prime powers) by a router on the ENTIRE exact tau=R/H_c. It keeps the residual exponent lambda-kappa at a content prime; none is discarded. Thus the adapter is valid even with empty relative-fresh M_rel.


Outside content the factor choice agrees with140's n_j. At an original139 relative-fresh p^lambda||m_i, its unique target remains F_i and m_i|q_i. Content primes can occur in two F factors, and no unit/exact-depth assertion is imported there from the fresh theorem. No identification of q_0 with a Gaussian all-same core is made without that route's coefficient/content adapter.


## 3. Same-height integral receiver and a large square divisor
Define signed integers zeta_j=F_j/q_j^2. They are nonzero; zeta_0 is positive. With exact R=H_c*tau,
 0<zeta_0<=6H_c^2(tau/q_0)^2,
 0<|zeta_i|<=4H_c^2(tau/q_i)^2 (i=1,2,3).
Since the q_j are odd, zeta_0=3 mod8 and zeta_i=1 mod8. A further retained global necessity is
 H_c^2 | product_(j=0..3)zeta_j,
obtained by dividing139's R^2|product F_j by tau^2. The other signed minus-square and monic139 conditions are still required; divisibility alone is not a physical converse.


At least one q_j>=tau^(1/4), so one of the four actual physical quadratic forms has an integer square divisor at least tau^(1/2). Its corresponding |zeta_j| is at most6H_c^2*tau^(3/2). This large-square-divisor alternative applies to full tau, with explicit content constants, and is not restricted to fresh support. It is a necessary same-R receiver, not a counting theorem.


For fixed A,R the allocation is canonical, so enlarging the tuple does not multiply endpoint counts. Counting arbitrary tuples A,q,zeta or arbitrary roots instead of realized endpoints requires all original masks plus139 signed integer reconstruction.138 uniform at-most8 physical inverse remains, and that fixed fiber is already consumed.


## 4. What is new, and what remains unproved
New: precise pair-content gcd bounds supply a complete integer tau adapter through content-supported prime powers; the large Heron square-divisor event therefore has no small-fresh-support escape at the level of this necessary cover.
Retained, not newly credited: primitive content formulas, generic R^2 divisor, root-line destination on fresh support, old four Gaussian core dichotomies and fixed-fiber bounds. The new integer receiver is not automatically theorem-equivalent to the older Gaussian inverse-fraction receiver; both keep their own original height/coefficient masks.


The cover does not prove enough scarcity of realized A for a fixed-power saving. The enlarged quadratic square-divisor event can have many nonphysical solutions. No independence, density multiplication, hidden B-uniform H_c constant, or automatic quantitative factor separation is asserted.140 full-factor saturation remains impossible at R, but q_j=tau can still occur when H_c>1; do not replace R by tau in that exclusion.

# M3-T11-142 — Linear-height nonphysical family defeats counting the bare Heron cover

## Authority and target
Fresh MAIN/INDEX/RESULT-LEDGER/active ROUTE141 and latest141, with140 proper factor/parity,139 signed integer reconstruction and138 physical projective height. No full-history reread. The question is whether141's content-complete large-square-divisor cover alone can furnish a sufficiently small moving support count. The answer for the enlarged integer cover is NO: an explicit fixed-content family has linear support in the same height window, while none of its points is physical.
This does not refute a count imposing the original T11 packet or the full139 signed/monic lift. Those additional conditions are not verified in this family. Preserve every established physical result and all credit/closure flags.


## 1. Explicit arithmetic progression and primitive plus-vector impostors
For k>=0, put
 n=241+8670k, R=17n,
 A=(6n+5,6n+3,3n+4).
The step8670=2*3*5*17^2. Thus n is odd, n=1 mod3 and5, n=241 mod289, and n is a17-unit.
Every A is positive and odd. A_1-A_2=2, so gcd(A_1,A_2)=1 and the triple is primitive.
